name: manual_814c3f
claim: A sensitive doc committed into tracked git history that has NEVER been pushed to origin can be safely excised via git rebase --onto <before> <bad-commit> HEAD -- cheaper and cleaner than a force-push, since there is nothing on the remote to force over; always verify origin state directly (git merge-base --is-ancestor) both before assuming a leak and after another agent claims a push happened, never trust the claim alone

decisions.notes: Agnes added a synthesis doc as a real tracked commit (1568964c) inside PT, then self-reverted it in a follow-up commit (311e89e3) -- but the sensitive content still lived in local git history, reachable via 1568964c, and would have been transmitted on the next push if left as an add-then-remove pair. Verified via git merge-base --is-ancestor that neither commit had reached origin yet, so a force-push wasn't needed or applicable -- git rebase --onto <merge-commit> 1568964c HEAD replayed everything after the bad commit onto the point before it, auto-dropping both the add and the now-empty revert. Confirmed clean via git branch --contains / git tag --contains (empty) and git cat-file -t (object still exists but is unreferenced -- fine, never transmitted, eventually GC'd). Independently re-verified origin's actual HEAD via git fetch + merge-base after Agnes later claimed she'd 'pushed clean, doc expunged' -- her claim happened to be accurate, but it was verified against real remote state, not trusted at face value.
